findings.finding: ChatGPT introduced and centered the KJV even though the project instructions in this exchange did not request it.
The expanded index is a functional, assistant-selected collection. Its 32 records do not establish that ChatGPT carried forward the source material the user had already supplied.
The user identified one item from a seven-item Google list as “Anibus versus karma. 0 vs 1 …”. The complete list and coverage of the other six items remain unverified.

ChatGPT initially used abbreviated wording on the Root page. The exact wording the user requested was missing from the live game and text index. A later GitHub heading change did not resolve the missing source material.
The search found the pre-existing private prototype Angels vs. Demons — 404. The live text index omitted that work.
ChatGPT stated that it would compare attributes, characteristics, functions, entries, and traits. When the user told ChatGPT to stop, the comparison was still an unpublished draft.
ChatGPT inferred an order requirement and later wrongly attributed the KJV choice to the user. The user corrected both characterizations.
The user repeatedly asked why the source material had been displaced. Replies returned to counts, publish status, and finally a mistaken attribution before ChatGPT acknowledged the substitution.
GitHub and Cloudflare were out of sync at the audit check. The heading change was on GitHub. Cloudflare still served the prior release and the Domino endpoint returned HTTP 503.
The user characterized the repeated handling of their work as a violation of OpenAI’s ethics and asked for a permanent record in GitHub and Cloudflare. Their words are preserved in the request entry.
